title: intent.md frontmatter
description: Schema for the frontmatter of intent.md, the canonical gating artifact for the plan phase. The gate engine checks only id (must match the ticket), status, cycle, approved_by and approval_evidence; the rest of this schema is what the writer module (jira-intake) produces and what the test suite validates the skill's examples against.

id.description: Ticket id this intent traces back to, e.g. a Jira key

cycle.description: Which pass through the loop this intent.md belongs to. Always 1 in this client's phase-graph (no loop-back phase), kept so a phase-graph that does loop doesn't need a schema change — the gate engine checks this against the project's phase-state.json so a stale intent.md left over from a previous cycle can't silently satisfy a later gate.

problem.description: What's wrong or missing, in the requester's own words

open_questions.description: Anything the schema wants but the source didn't have. Must be empty, or explicitly waived, before define can close.

source.description: Which module filled the plan.intake capability slot for this project

prd_source.description: Set only when source is prd-import — a git ref back to the originating project's spec.md/intent.md

epic.description: Parent Jira epic key this ticket was decomposed from, if any (e.g. a client whose own tooling breaks a PRD/RFC into epics and stories in Jira). Absent when the ticket has no parent epic.

source_docs.description: Links back to the PRD/RFC (or equivalent) the parent epic was decomposed from, when the epic carries them. Lets Define/Design pull the full product context instead of just this one story's isolated fields — set by jira-intake when the epic has them, left empty otherwise rather than guessed.

skip_reason.description: Why define/design were skipped. Required in practice on the fast-track track (phase-graph.yaml's `fast-track.requires: skip_reason`) — that track goes plan -> develop -> launch, so this frontmatter field is the only place the reason for skipping two gates is ever recorded. Set it from the routed track (start-ticket's output / phase-state.json's `track`), not from a guess. Leave unset on standard, where nothing was skipped.

approval_evidence.description: Required when status is approved (require_approval_evidence in phase-graph.yaml) — a link to the Jira comment/Slack message/email where this was actually approved. The product owner approving this rarely has git/GitHub/Cursor/Claude access at all; this is what makes approved_by checkable instead of just a transcribed name.

approvals.description: One entry per approving role. Only needed when this artifact's gate asks for more than one signature (a quorum or tier strategy in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml). A single-approver gate keeps using status/approved_by/approval_evidence. Every entry needs its own evidence link when require_approval_evidence is on — one link does not cover two people.

role.description: The approval role named by this gate in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml, e.g. product_owner. An entry for a role the gate did not ask for does not count toward it.

by.description: The person who decided. Required when status is approved.

evidence.description: Link to where this person actually approved or declined — the Jira comment, Slack message or change record.
